title: Jeremiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 43 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 43.

questions.question: Who spoke against Jeremiah, claiming he was lying?
questions.correctAnswer: Azariah
questions.explanation: Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, along with Johanan and other proud men, spoke against Jeremiah, as stated in Jeremiah 43:2.

questions.question: What did the proud men accuse Jeremiah of?
options: Telling them to go to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking falsely
questions.explanation: The proud men, including Azariah and Johanan, accused Jeremiah of speaking falsely, as noted in Jeremiah 43:2.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was accused of trying to deliver the people into the hands of the Chaldeans.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The accusation that Baruch was setting Jeremiah against the people to deliver them to the Chaldeans is found in Jeremiah 43:3.

questions.question: Who did Johanan and the captains of the forces not obey?
questions.correctAnswer: The voice of the LORD
questions.explanation: Johanan and the captains did not obey the voice of the LORD as mentioned in Jeremiah 43:4.

questions.question: What did Johanan take with him to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Men, women, and children
questions.explanation: Johanan took all the remnant of Judah, which included men, women, children, and the king's daughters, as stated in Jeremiah 43:5.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Judah obeyed the voice of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The people did not obey the voice of the LORD and instead went to Egypt, indicating their disobedience as noted in Jeremiah 43:4.

questions.question: Where did the remnant of Judah come from before going to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: All nations
questions.explanation: The remnant of Judah had returned from all nations whither they had been driven, as stated in Jeremiah 43:5.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was left in the land of Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was indeed left in the land of Judah along with Baruch, as mentioned in Jeremiah 43:6.

questions.question: What instruction did the LORD give to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes?
questions.correctAnswer: To take great stones
questions.explanation: The LORD instructed Jeremiah to take great stones and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln in Tahpanhes, as stated in Jeremiah 43:9.

questions.question: What will Nebuchadrezzar do when he comes to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Smite the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: The prophecy states that Nebuchadrezzar shall smite the land of Egypt, as noted in Jeremiah 43:11.

questions.question: In what location did the people of Judah come to according to the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Tahpanhes
questions.explanation: The people of Judah came to Tahpanhes as they disobeyed the voice of the LORD, which is mentioned in Jeremiah 43:7.

questions.question: True or False: The houses of the gods of Egypt will be burned.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The LORD proclaims that Nebuchadrezzar will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt and burn them, as stated in Jeremiah 43:12.

questions.question: What will Nebuchadrezzar array himself with?
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Egypt
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that he shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as stated in Jeremiah 43:12.

questions.question: What will happen to the images of Bethshemesh in Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be broken
questions.explanation: The prophecy states that Nebuchadrezzar shall break the images of Bethshemesh in the land of Egypt, as mentioned in Jeremiah 43:13.

questions.question: In what order did the events occur after Jeremiah spoke to the people?
options: The proud men spoke against Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: The proud men spoke against Jeremiah
questions.explanation: The proud men spoke against Jeremiah immediately after he finished speaking to the people, as stated in Jeremiah 43:1-2.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 43 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were taken by Johanan and the captains of the forces to dwell in Egypt?
options: Men, women, children, king's daughters, and those left by Nebuzaradan with Gedaliah, Jeremiah, and Baruch
Only men and captains of the forces
Only the king's daughters and Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: Men, women, children, king's daughters, and those left by Nebuzaradan with Gedaliah, Jeremiah, and Baruch
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:6 states that Johanan took men, women, children, king's daughters, and every person left by Nebuzaradan with Gedaliah, Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch to Egypt. This shows the inclusiveness of the group that disobeyed God's command.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 43:7, why did the people come to Tahpanhes in Egypt?
options: Because they obeyed not the voice of the LORD
Because they were invited by Pharaoh
Because Jeremiah commanded them to go
Because they sought refuge from the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: Because they obeyed not the voice of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:7 explains that the people came into Egypt and reached Tahpanhes because they disobeyed the voice of the LORD. This disobedience is the reason for their relocation to Egypt, rather than following God's instructions to remain in Judah.

questions.question: What specific action did the LORD command Jeremiah to perform at the brickkiln at Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes?
options: Take great stones and hide them in the clay
Build an altar and offer sacrifices
Pray publicly for the people of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Take great stones and hide them in the clay
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:9 instructs Jeremiah to take great stones and hide them in clay in the brickkiln at Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes. This prophetic act was meant to symbolize the future establishment of Nebuchadnezzar's throne there.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 43:10 demonstrate God's sovereignty over kings and nations?
options: God declares that Nebuchadnezzar, his servant, will set his throne on the hidden stones
God tells Jeremiah to curse the king of Babylon
God allows Pharaoh to defeat Nebuchadnezzar
God remains silent about the fate of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: God declares that Nebuchadnezzar, his servant, will set his throne on the hidden stones
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:10 shows God's sovereignty by declaring that Nebuchadnezzar, whom God refers to as His servant, will set his throne on the stones Jeremiah hid. This indicates God's control over even foreign rulers and their destiny.

questions.question: What is promised to happen to Egypt when Nebuchadnezzar comes, according to Jeremiah 43:11?
options: The land will be smitten, and people will face death, captivity, or the sword
Egypt will be spared and prosper
Pharaoh will defeat Nebuchadnezzar and expand his kingdom
Egypt will form an alliance with Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The land will be smitten, and people will face death, captivity, or the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:11 states that when Nebuchadnezzar comes, he will smite Egypt and bring death, captivity, and the sword upon those destined for such. This fulfills God's judgment against Egypt for harboring the disobedient remnant.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 43:12 say God will do to the gods of Egypt during Nebuchadnezzar's invasion?
options: Kindle a fire to burn their houses and carry them away captives
Cause the gods to protect Egypt
Remove the gods from the land peacefully
Restore the gods after the invasion
questions.correctAnswer: Kindle a fire to burn their houses and carry them away captives
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:12 describes God's judgment by kindling a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, burning them, and carrying them captive. This symbolizes the defeat of Egypt's false gods along with the nation.

questions.question: How does the passage of Jeremiah 43:6-7 illustrate the consequences of disobedience to God's voice?
options: The people disobeyed and fled to Egypt, resulting in judgment and captivity
The people obeyed and were blessed with peace
The people were protected from Babylon by God's intervention
The people were immediately forgiven and restored
questions.correctAnswer: The people disobeyed and fled to Egypt, resulting in judgment and captivity
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 show that the people ignored God's command to stay in Judah and instead went to Egypt, disobeying the LORD. This act of disobedience led to the prophecy of Babylonian judgment and captivity described in later verses.

questions.question: What lesson about trust in God's guidance can be drawn from the actions of Johanan and the captains in Jeremiah 43:4-5?
options: Ignoring God's word leads to detrimental decisions, like fleeing to Egypt
Following human leaders is always better than trusting God
Disobedience to God results in immediate success and safety
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring God's word leads to detrimental decisions, like fleeing to Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:4-5 reveals that Johanan and the military captains did not obey the LORD's command to remain in Judah, instead taking the people to Egypt. This decision, prompted by distrust and disobedience, led to further judgment and hardship.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jeremiah 43:8, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah while he was in Egypt at Tahpanhes.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:8 explicitly states that the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, which is in Egypt. This shows that God's prophetic communication continued even in foreign lands.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 43:10 teach about God's use of human rulers to accomplish His purposes?
options: God calls Nebuchadnezzar His servant and uses him to fulfill divine judgment
God rejects all foreign kings and leaves the nations to their own devices
God only uses Israelite kings for His plans
God punishes rulers who act against Him
questions.correctAnswer: God calls Nebuchadnezzar His servant and uses him to fulfill divine judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:10 refers to Nebuchadnezzar as 'my servant,' indicating that God sovereignly uses even foreign kings to carry out His purposes, such as judgment on Egypt and Israel's enemies.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 43:9-10, what is the significance of Jeremiah hiding stones in the brickkiln before Pharaoh's house?
options: It symbolizes the future establishment of Nebuchadnezzar's throne there as God's judgment
It was a secret treasure for the people of Judah
It was a ritual to appease the gods of Egypt
It was an act of rebellion against Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the future establishment of Nebuchadnezzar's throne there as God's judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:9-10 describes a prophetic sign where Jeremiah hides stones in clay at the brickkiln. God declares Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne on these stones, symbolizing Babylon's future dominion over Egypt as part of divine judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 43:3 suggests that Baruch was trying to help the people by delivering them into the hand of the Chaldeans.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:3 states that the people accused Baruch of setting Jeremiah against them to hand them over to the Chaldeans for death and captivity. This was a false accusation by the people, not Baruch's intention.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 43:12-13, what will Nebuchadnezzar do to the images of Bethshemesh and the houses of the gods in Egypt?
options: Break the images and burn the houses of the gods with fire
Restore them to their former glory
Sell them as treasures in Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Break the images and burn the houses of the gods with fire
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 describe that Nebuchadnezzar will break the images of Bethshemesh and burn the houses of the Egyptian gods. This symbolizes the comprehensive judgment against Egypt's idolatry.

questions.question: What does the narrative in Jeremiah 43 teach about the importance of obedience to God's commands?
options: Disobedience leads to judgment and hardship, while obedience aligns with God's plan
Obedience is optional and has no consequences
God punishes those who obey more than those who disobey
Obedience guarantees worldly success without challenges
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to judgment and hardship, while obedience aligns with God's plan
questions.explanation: The chapter shows that the people’s disobedience in fleeing to Egypt brought judgment (Jeremiah 43:7,11), while God's commands aim to protect and guide His people (43:1,4). Obedience is essential for following God’s purpose.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 43:2 shows that some leaders accused Jeremiah of falsely claiming he was sent by the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:2 records Azariah, Johanan, and other proud men accusing Jeremiah of speaking falsely and denying that the LORD sent him to warn against going into Egypt.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 43.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Johanan the son of Kareah and the proud men to Jeremiah's prophecy about not going into Egypt?
options: They accused Jeremiah of speaking falsely
They asked for a sign from God
questions.correctAnswer: They accused Jeremiah of speaking falsely
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:2 states that Azariah, Johanan, and the proud men said Jeremiah spoke falsely and that the LORD had not sent him to say not to go into Egypt.

questions.question: Who did Johanan and the captains take with them when they disobeyed the LORD and went to Egypt?
options: Only the king's daughters and Baruch
All the remnant of Judah returned from all nations, including men, women, children, the king's daughters, Jeremiah, and Baruch
questions.correctAnswer: All the remnant of Judah returned from all nations, including men, women, children, the king's daughters, Jeremiah, and Baruch
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:5-6 shows that Johanan took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all nations, including the king's daughters, Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch.

questions.question: Where did the people go after disobeying the LORD's command?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt, specifically Tahpanhes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:7 states that they went into the land of Egypt and came to Tahpanhes, disobeying the voice of the LORD.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Jeremiah to do with great stones at Tahpanhes?
options: Hide them in clay in the brickkiln at Pharaoh's house
Throw them into the Nile river
Use them to build a wall around the city
questions.correctAnswer: Hide them in clay in the brickkiln at Pharaoh's house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:9 commands Jeremiah to take great stones and hide them in clay in the brickkiln at the entry of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 43:10, who is Nebuchadrezzar described as?
questions.correctAnswer: The servant of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:10 refers to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon as the LORD's servant who will set his throne upon the stones.

questions.question: What will Nebuchadrezzar do when he comes to Egypt, according to Jeremiah 43:11?
options: He will make peace with Egypt
He will smite the land and execute judgment by death, captivity, and sword
He will build temples to Egyptian gods
He will flee the land in fear
questions.correctAnswer: He will smite the land and execute judgment by death, captivity, and sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:11 states Nebuchadrezzar will smite Egypt, delivering those meant for death to death, captivity to captivity, and sword to sword.

questions.question: What will happen to the gods and their houses in Egypt as prophesied in Jeremiah 43:12?
options: They will be honored and protected
They will be destroyed by fire and the people carried into captivity
They will be relocated to Babylon
They will be hidden from Nebuchadrezzar
questions.correctAnswer: They will be destroyed by fire and the people carried into captivity
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:12 says the LORD will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, burn them, carry captives away, and Nebuchadrezzar will go forth in peace.

questions.question: What specific location's images will Nebuchadrezzar break in Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Bethshemesh
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:13 states that Nebuchadrezzar will break the images of Bethshemesh in Egypt and burn the houses of their gods.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage similarly prophesies the destruction of Egypt by Nebuchadnezzar?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 19
questions.explanation: Isaiah 19 similarly predicts the judgment and turmoil in Egypt, paralleling Jeremiah 43's prophecy of Nebuchadnezzar's conquest (Jeremiah 43:11-13; Isaiah 19:1-17).

questions.question: The phrase 'as a shepherd putteth on his garment' in Jeremiah 43:12 is an example of which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:12 uses a simile comparing Nebuchadrezzar's taking possession of Egypt to a shepherd putting on a garment.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'captain of the guard' in Jeremiah 43:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Sar
questions.explanation: 'Sar' in Hebrew means chief or captain, indicating a military leader as used in Jeremiah 43:6 referring to Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's servant used to bring judgment as seen in Nebuchadrezzar's role in Jeremiah 43?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 13:1-7
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1-7 speaks of governing authorities as God's servants to execute wrath on evildoers, paralleling Nebuchadrezzar as God's servant in Jeremiah 43:10-11.

questions.question: What was the original audience's likely perception of Nebuchadrezzar's coming to Egypt as described in Jeremiah 43?
options: A sign of God's judgment and impending doom
questions.correctAnswer: A sign of God's judgment and impending doom
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43 addresses the remnant of Judah who disobeyed God; Nebuchadrezzar's coming symbolized divine judgment upon Egypt and disobedient Judah (Jeremiah 43:10-13).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was persuaded by Baruch to go into Egypt with the remnant of Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:3 shows Baruch was accused of setting Jeremiah against the people, but Jeremiah himself did not persuade them to go; they disobeyed the LORD's command.

questions.question: True or False: The prophecy in Jeremiah 43 includes a message of peace after Nebuchadrezzar's conquest of Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:12 ends with Nebuchadrezzar going forth from Egypt in peace after judgment and destruction.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 43 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 43 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the reason Azariah and Johanan accused Jeremiah of speaking falsely?
options: Because he said they should not go into Egypt to sojourn there
Because he told them to fight against Babylon
Because he claimed Nebuchadnezzar would be defeated
Because he prophesied peace for Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Because he said they should not go into Egypt to sojourn there
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:2 records that Azariah and Johanan accused Jeremiah of falsehood because he told them the LORD had not sent him to say, 'Go not into Egypt to sojourn there.' This shows their rejection of God's command regarding Egypt.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 43, who did Baruch allegedly set Jeremiah against?
questions.correctAnswer: The people of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:3 explains that Baruch was said to have set Jeremiah against the people of Judah, intending to deliver them into the hands of the Chaldeans for death and captivity.

questions.question: What was the people's response to the LORD's command to dwell in the land of Judah?
options: They obeyed and stayed in Judah
They ignored the command and went to Egypt
They returned to Jerusalem to rebuild
questions.correctAnswer: They ignored the command and went to Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:4 shows that Johanan, the captains, and all the people disobeyed the LORD's voice to dwell in Judah; instead, they moved to Egypt as recorded in verse 7.

questions.question: Which group of people did Johanan and the captains take with them to Egypt?
options: All the remnant of Judah returned from all nations
questions.correctAnswer: All the remnant of Judah returned from all nations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:5 states that Johanan and the captains took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from various nations, including men, women, children, and the king’s daughters.

questions.question: Who were left in Judah by Nebuzaradan and Gedaliah according to Jeremiah 43?
options: Men, women, children, king’s daughters, Jeremiah, and Baruch
Only the captains of the forces
None were left, all were taken to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Men, women, children, king’s daughters, Jeremiah, and Baruch
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:6 clarifies that Nebuzaradan the captain left men, women, children, king's daughters, Jeremiah the prophet, and Baruch with Gedaliah in Judah.

questions.question: Where did the people go after disobeying the LORD's command to stay in Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt, to Tahpanhes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:7 states explicitly that they went into Egypt and came to Tahpanhes, disobeying God's voice to remain in Judah.

questions.question: What symbolic action did the LORD command Jeremiah to perform in Tahpanhes?
options: Hide great stones in clay in the brickkiln at Pharaoh’s house
Build an altar to the LORD
Write a scroll of judgment against Egypt
Burn incense before the Egyptian gods
questions.correctAnswer: Hide great stones in clay in the brickkiln at Pharaoh’s house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:9 instructs Jeremiah to take great stones and hide them in clay in the brickkiln at the entry of Pharaoh’s house, symbolizing judgment to come.

questions.question: What does the LORD declare He will do with Nebuchadrezzar in Jeremiah 43?
options: Set his throne upon the hidden stones and spread his royal pavilion over them
Give him a peaceful reign over Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Set his throne upon the hidden stones and spread his royal pavilion over them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:10 reveals God's sovereign control by declaring He will set Nebuchadrezzar's throne upon the stones Jeremiah hid, showing Babylon’s dominion even over Egypt.

questions.question: What judgment will Nebuchadrezzar bring upon Egypt according to Jeremiah 43?
options: Death to those for death, captivity to those for captivity, and sword to those for the sword
A covenant of alliance with Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Death to those for death, captivity to those for captivity, and sword to those for the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:11 states that Nebuchadrezzar will execute divine justice by bringing death, captivity, and the sword according to the judgment decreed by God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God sending Nebuchadrezzar to judge Egypt as described in Jeremiah 43?
options: God’s omniscience in predicting the future
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in executing punishment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:11-12 displays God's justice attribute by sending Nebuchadrezzar to punish Egypt for their sins, a clear expression of divine retribution.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 43:12 reveal God's sovereignty over idols?
options: God will kindle fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt and burn them
God will make the idols worship Him
God will hide the idols to protect them
questions.correctAnswer: God will kindle fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt and burn them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:12 shows God's sovereignty over false gods by prophesying their destruction by fire, revealing the LORD’s power over idols that cannot save.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Jeremiah 43:4 and Jeremiah 43:7 provide about human disobedience?
options: Human disobedience leads to judgment and exile
God abandons His people when they disobey
questions.correctAnswer: Human disobedience leads to judgment and exile
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:4 and 43:7 together show that the people’s disobedience to God's command to remain in Judah resulted in their exile to Egypt, illustrating the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.

questions.question: What theological truth emerges from combining Jeremiah 43:9 and Jeremiah 43:10 about God's control over history?
options: God sovereignly ordains earthly rulers to fulfill His purposes
God is powerless over political events
Human kings act independently of God’s will
God's plans are unclear and unpredictable
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains earthly rulers to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:9-10 illustrates that God orchestrates historical events by using Nebuchadrezzar as His servant to execute judgment, affirming divine sovereignty over human authority.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 43:5-6 together deepen our understanding of God's preservation of a faithful remnant?
options: God preserves a remnant even amid judgment and exile
God rejects all those who disobey
God only cares for the priests and king
God's promises are only for the land of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves a remnant even amid judgment and exile
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 show that despite widespread judgment, God preserves a remnant of Judah—men, women, children, even the king's daughters—highlighting God's faithfulness to His covenant people.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s prophecy in Jeremiah 43 about Nebuchadrezzar’s conquest of Egypt is unreliable. What does Jeremiah 43:10-13 actually teach about God’s prophetic authority?
options: God accurately predicts future events, displaying His sovereign authority
God’s prophecies are vague and open-ended
God’s word depends on human interpretation
God’s prophecies are symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God accurately predicts future events, displaying His sovereign authority
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 43:10-13 demonstrates God's prophetic authority by precisely foretelling Nebuchadrezzar’s invasion and destruction of Egyptian gods and land, affirming divine omniscience and sovereignty (cf. Isaiah 46:9-10).
